figures.alt: Robert W. Weir's 1843 painting Embarkation of the Pilgrims — Pilgrims praying on the deck of the Speedwell around an open Bible, with a rainbow and a sail reading 'God with us'
figures.caption: Embarkation of the Pilgrims, Robert W. Weir, 1843

books.section: The Pilgrims and the Massachusetts Bay Company

parts.modelAnswer: The painting shows a group of Pilgrims praying on the deck of the ship Speedwell in 1620, gathered around an open Bible. A rainbow arches behind them and the sail above reads 'God with us.'

scoring.criterion: Earns the point for identifying what the painting shows, such as Pilgrims praying on the Speedwell in 1620 around an open Bible.
scoring.notEarned: Naming only the artist or the date, with no description of the scene, does not earn the point.

parts.modelAnswer: The painting presents the Pilgrims as a solemn, prayerful band of families chosen by God — the open Bible, the rainbow, and the words 'God with us' all mark them as a holy founding. That is how 19th-century Americans liked to remember them, as the pious founders of the nation.
parts.prompt: Explain how the painting reflects the way 19th-century Americans remembered the Pilgrims.

scoring.criterion: Earns the point for explaining how the painting reflects 19th-century memory, such as the Pilgrims as pious, God-chosen founders of the nation.
scoring.notEarned: Describing the scene without connecting it to 19th-century memory does not earn the point.

parts.modelAnswer: Weir painted it in 1843, more than two hundred years after the event, so he never saw the departure and imagined the scene. The painting is a 19th-century idea of the Pilgrims, not a record of what the departure actually looked like.
parts.prompt: Explain one limitation of the painting as evidence about the Pilgrims' departure.

scoring.criterion: Earns the point for explaining one limitation, such as the painting being made in 1843, over two hundred years after the event, by an artist who imagined the scene rather than recording it.
scoring.notEarned: Stating only that the painting is old, with no limitation explained, does not earn the point.

stimulus.text: Robert W. Weir, Embarkation of the Pilgrims, 1843. On the deck of the ship Speedwell, a group of Pilgrims kneels and stands in prayer around an open Bible, with a rainbow behind them and a sail above bearing the words 'God with us.' Armor and a musket lie on the deck in the foreground, and a soldier kneels at the right. The painting hangs in the Rotunda of the United States Capitol.
